posts.name: The Burning Stickman
posts.cooked:
So I've been playing against AOG Spite in the video game, and it just seems impossible to get enough Victim cards A. in play and B. under the Safe House to make his drug cards flip back without making Spite flip. Because of the order of operations, he always starts with one Drug card flipped and one Victim card out. Then, at best, he plays another victim card. Even if you put both of them under the Safe House that turn, he's going to flip another Drug card at the start of the turn, and since it's now equal to what's under the safe house, neither of them will flip back. Even if he plays another victim card, there's still no way to get ahead of the curve.

And once he's got three drug cards flipped face up, there's just plain no way to get any of them flipped back before he flips to his other side.

So am I missing something? Outside of forcing him to play cards, which only applies to a tiny handful of heroes and one or two environments, there doesn't seem to be any way to get ahead of the drug curve.

posts.name: Ronway
posts.cooked: He starts with a victim and plays another. One of which has to be a Good Samaritan and the other has to be any of the other Victims. Over the course of the hero's turns, save the other victim, at the start of the Environment turn you save the Good Samaritan and if it plays a Good Samaritan you can save that one aswell. If another victim is played, then you now have 3 Victims under the Safehouse. At the start of his turn he'll either flip his Character Cards if (H) = 3 or he'll Flip a drug at the start face-up and then flip a face-up one back face-down at the end.

posts.cooked: This is one of the few places where I will go ahead and say "bad game design". Devoting that much verbiage to a condition that is almost impossible to bring about is just broken. And it would be easy to fix; if instead of "more" the condition was "at least as many as", it would be plausibly achievable far more often.

posts.name: The Burning Stickman
posts.cooked:
It just seems like such an absurdly narrow circumstance to flip his cards back.

I tend to play 5 heroes because I like using a lot of them, but the times I've tried fighting against him, I can't gain any traction because having to put back 3 ongoings every turn makes it so you have to do nothing but play ongoings and equipments just to keep up (Damaging or utility one-shots? Ain't nobody got time for that), 3 DR is really hard to get past even if it's only once a turn and and when you do manage to damage him, destroying the Victim cards still heals him.

It seems like he can only go one of two ways -- a long, torturous slog where the only variable is which of his painful drugs flips first, you get extremely lucky with the card draw, or you play an extremely specific party (one member of which is not yet part of the video game) and get lucky with the card draw to neuter him.

It's just...frustrating and not fun.
